name: TL7705AIDR
title: TL77xxA supply-voltage supervisors (TL7702A, TL7705A, TL7709A, TL7712A, TL7715A)
summary: Five reset controllers for microprocessor systems. Each watches a supply on SENSE and, when it drops below the threshold, drives a pair of complementary reset outputs (RESET high, /RESET low); after the supply recovers, the outputs are held for a delay set by one capacitor on CT. The TL7705A, TL7709A, TL7712A and TL7715A trip at 4.55, 7.6, 10.8 and 13.5 V; the TL7702A has a bare 2.53 V comparator set by an external divider. A 2.53 V reference is brought out on REF. TL7702ACDR is the TL7702A, 0 °C to 70 °C, in SOIC-8 on a 2500-piece reel.
key_figures: 3.5 V to 18 V (20 V absolute max)
2.48 V min, 2.53 V typ, 2.58 V max
td = 1.3 × 10^4 × CT; 1.2 ms typ at CT = 0.1 µF
RESET sources 16 mA; /RESET sinks 16 mA at 0.4 V max

notes: C parts run from 0 °C to 70 °C, I parts from −40 °C to 85 °C. D is SOIC-8, P is PDIP-8, PS is SO-8; R marks tape and reel. All are RoHS and in production.
TL7712AIDR lists its operating temperature as "-"; TL7712AIDR.A lists 0 to 70.

circuits.title: Reset controller for a 5 V microprocessor
circuits.description: A TL7705A watches the 5 V rail that also feeds the microcontroller. SENSE and /RESIN both sit on 5 V. /RESET, held up by a 10 kΩ resistor to 5 V, goes to the controller's reset pin; the active-high RESET output is used only with a 10 kΩ resistor to ground. CT of 0.1 µF gives a delay of about 1.3 ms, and 0.1 µF on REF filters the reference.
notes: Design targets: 5 V supply, td = 1.3 ms. CT (F) = td (s) / (1.3 × 10^4).

circuits.title: Reset from three supplies: 12 V, 5 V and −12 V
circuits.description: Three supervisors share one system reset. A TL7712A on the 12 V rail and a TL7712A that runs between ground and −12 V (its VCC, SENSE and /RESIN on ground, its GND pin on −12 V) both pull down a node held up to 5 V by 22 kΩ; the −12 V unit reaches it through 10 kΩ, and a diode sits on the node with its anode at ground. That node drives /RESIN of a TL7705A on the 5 V rail, whose /RESET, pulled up by 10 kΩ, is the system reset. Each RESET output carries a 10 kΩ resistor to its own GND pin, and each part has its own CT and a 0.1 µF REF capacitor.

circuits.title: Reset with no undefined state, P-channel JFET
circuits.description: The TL7705A is powered from the unregulated input ahead of a µA7805 and senses the regulator's 5 V output. /RESET, pulled up to the input by 4.7 kΩ, drives the gate of a 2N3994 P-channel JFET whose source is the system /RESET line, pulled up to 5 V by 25 kΩ, and whose drain is grounded. RESET has a 4.7 kΩ load to ground; /RESIN has no connection.

parts.note: P-channel JFET; its case lead is tied to the drain

circuits.title: Reset with no undefined state, PNP transistor
circuits.description: SENSE takes the voltage to be watched while the TL77xxA runs from VCC, with /RESIN tied to VCC. RESET drives a 2N4036 PNP through a divider: 750 Ω from VCC to the base, 2.7 kΩ from the base to RESET, and 10 kΩ from RESET to ground. The emitter is on VCC and the collector, with 1 kΩ to ground, is the system /RESET. /RESET has only a 10 kΩ pull-up to VCC.

where.td: delay after SENSE (or /RESIN) recovers before the outputs release, s
where.CT: capacitor from CT to GND, F

operation.text: The TL77xxA holds a processor in reset while its supply is low. SENSE is compared with an internal threshold. When SENSE drops below VIT−, RESET goes high and /RESET goes low. When SENSE comes back above VIT+ (VIT− plus the hysteresis), the outputs stay active for a delay td set by the capacitor on CT and are then released, so every reset lasts at least td.

TL7705A trips at 4.55 V and suits 5 V logic and microcomputer rails. TL7709A trips at 7.6 V. TL7712A trips at 10.8 V for 12 V CMOS, processor and memory rails. TL7715A trips at 13.5 V for 15 V analog rails. TL7702A has a 2.5 V threshold (VIT− 2.53 V typ) with no internal divider; an external divider on SENSE sets the trip point for any other rail.

Below Vres the outputs are undefined; Vres is 3 V maximum, 2.5 V typical. From Vres up, CT is held discharged and the outputs are active (RESET high, /RESET low). /RESET goes active as VCC nears 3.6 V, the lowest supply at which operation is guaranteed. Once SENSE passes the threshold, an internal thyristor across CT turns off, CT charges, and after td the voltage on CT crosses the output comparator's trip level and both outputs go inactive.
With SENSE under VIT−, the outputs stay active as VCC falls, down to about 2 V. Below that they are undefined.

/RESIN low (under 0.6 V) forces reset; propagation from /RESIN to /RESET is 1 µs max at VCC = 5 V, and a /RESIN pulse must be at least 0.4 µs. When /RESIN returns above 2 V the outputs are held active for td. On SENSE, a dip of 200 mV under VIT− must last 2 µs to switch the outputs.
td = 1.3 × 10^4 × CT, with CT in farads and td in seconds; 0.1 µF gives 1.3 ms nominal (0.65 ms to 2.6 ms over the specified range). Inside, a current source of about 100 µA charges CT.

The 2.53 V reference on REF is temperature compensated and may be used as a reference elsewhere. It moves less than 10 mV over VCC from 3.5 V to 18 V and 16 mV over −40 °C to 85 °C. A capacitor, typically 0.1 µF, is required on REF to reduce the effect of fast supply transients.

The outputs are open collector: /RESET needs a pull-up resistor for a defined high level. RESET sources up to 16 mA with VOH at least VCC − 1.5 V; /RESET sinks up to 16 mA at 0.4 V max. The 5 V design example uses 10 kΩ on each output.
Specified from 3.5 V to 18 V. More than 20 V on VCC can damage the part.

Keep the supervisor away from circuits that switch large currents, such as bus interfaces and power switches. SENSE, CT and REF are analog nodes. Noise on CT shortens the reset pulse; noise on REF or its capacitor can trip the part and give an unwanted reset, most often when heavy currents share the ground return of these capacitors. Run the CT and REF capacitor grounds straight and short to the GND pin, with no other circuit's current in them. On the TL7702A, place the SENSE divider resistors so noise cannot couple into them.
In the example board the timing capacitor Ct and the reference capacitor Cref sit next to pins 3 and 1 and both return straight to pin 4, where GND enters.
